notice: PROPOSED DRAFT for owner review. Not committed: committed_at is a placeholder, so the manifest validator refuses it and no paid trial may use it until the owner edits and commits it.
title: Research report with sources: a fixed question about a pinned repository snapshot, answered with checkable citations

fixture.snapshot: the pinned monomind commit named in the trial manifest, read-only, no network
fixture.question: How does an org session decide when to end and start a fresh one, and what does each path record? Cover: (1) the task-scope boundary, (2) the idle exit, (3) the budget stops, (4) the session cap. Name the file and function behind each claim.

units.description: A report answering the fixed question, one section per sub-question, every claim cited as path:line
units.evidence: every citation resolves in the snapshot and the quoted text appears at the cited line (machine check); each of the four sub-questions has a section

units.description: A ledger of every citation with the claim it supports and the verbatim quote
units.evidence: each ledger row's quote is found verbatim at its path:line in the snapshot; row count equals the report's citation count

completion_rule: Both units present and accepted, with all four sub-questions covered. A padded ledger, citations repeated to raise the count, or one section answering two sub-questions adds nothing.

criteria.description: Every substantive claim carries a citation that resolves to the stated line
What the report says the cited code does is what it does
All four sub-questions are answered, including what each path records
No section is padding; nothing restates another section

critical_failures: a citation whose path or line does not exist in the snapshot
a quote that does not appear at its cited line
a claim about behaviour the cited code does not have

allowed_recovery: automatic restart of a crashed role within the runtime's retry limits
one operator answer to a blocking question, recorded as an intervention

primary_comparisons: cost per accepted unit, candidate vs matched baseline, paired by run
probability of a fully accepted fixture, with its Wilson interval
fabricated or unresolvable citations per run
